root_cause.text: `rb_read_data_buffer()` in `kernel/trace/ring_buffer.c` advanced through ring-buffer events by calling `rb_event_length(event)` before validating that the event header/length was sane, so a corrupted boot-time ring buffer could supply an invalid length and make `e + len` point outside the data page.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the loop from `for (e = 0; e < tail; e += rb_event_length(event))` to computing `len = rb_event_length(event)` first and rejecting `len <= 0 || len > tail - e` before using it, and the commit message says the function validates “possibly broken ring buffers” where “the length of the event could be broken” and `e + len` “can point a wrong address,” causing invalid memory access at boot.

intent_record.intent_summary: Validate ring buffer event lengths during parsing to prevent out-of-bounds iteration on corrupt data.
intent_record.what: The loop in `rb_read_data_buffer()` was changed to increment by a separate `len` variable instead of calling `rb_event_length(event)` in the `for` statement. Inside the loop, `len` is now assigned from `rb_event_length(event)`, and a new validation check was added to վերադարձ `-1` if `len <= 0` or if `len > tail - e`.
intent_record.how: This makes event parsing safer by validating each ring buffer event length before advancing. It prevents the code from stepping past the valid data range or looping incorrectly on malformed or zero-length events, and causes the function to fail early when the buffer contents are invalid.

candidates.rationale: This loop advances the iterator using rb_event_length(event) before any validation of the event header/length, so a corrupted event can cause the offset to jump past the data page and trigger out-of-bounds access.

This dereference occurs as part of the iteration that trusts the current offset and the previously computed length; with a malformed length the next event pointer can be derived from invalid in-page data.

The parser reads the event header only after the loop has already advanced by rb_event_length(event), so if the current event is corrupt the code may already have moved outside the valid buffer before this validation point.

The root cause was that `rb_read_data_buffer()` advanced with `for (e = 0; e < tail; e += rb_event_length(event))` and only then inspected `event->type_len`, meaning an invalid/corrupted event length could make `e + len` walk outside the data page. In this commit, that exact loop still exists inside the new helper: `for (e = 0; e < tail; e += rb_event_length(event)) { event = (struct ring_buffer_event *)(dpage->data + e); ... }`, so the vulnerable construct is present. However, the commit also adds validation around it: `rb_validate_buffer()` calls `rb_read_data_buffer()` and `rb_meta_validate_events()` resets invalid buffers, and `check_buffer()` now calls `rb_read_data_buffer()` instead of open-coding the walk. So the code includes the fix for boot-time range validation by validating metadata/events before trusting the buffer, even though the helper itself still uses `rb_event_length(event)` in the same traversal pattern.
